scope: Theorem 7.5 (Existence on finite truncations) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 54. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the prepared domain of Proposition 4.7 and every sufficiently small fixed ϵ > 0, there is an integer n0 ≥ 4 and, for each n ≥ n0, a radius Rmin(n), with Rmin(n) → ∞, such that the original deformation system has a smooth solution on every ΩR with R ≥ Rmin(n). It satisfies t > −ϵ on the closure. At fixed n, these solutions have the local bounds of Proposition 7.3, uniformly as R → ∞. In particular, any sequence Rj → ∞ of such radii has a subsequence converging smoothly on compact subsets of Ω to a solution of the original equations with t ≥ −ϵ.
